As a Portfolio Analytics & Strategy Analyst within the Real Estate Market Analytics (REMA) group you will be responsible for vetting real estate collateral for potential and existing PNC loans prior to ordering a third-party appraisal. Emphasis is placed on prospective asset performance due to a large level of new construction lending. Analyst will cross-check forward-looking developer proformas with existing market performance using industry leading data sources such as CoStar, CBRE-EA, MSCI, Yardi Matrix etc. and forecast future results. Forecasts include absorption (during lease-up), stabilized vacancy, market rent, rent growth, and concessions. Analyst must have a strong understanding of how local submarket performance is impacted by both MSA/regional and national economic trends and how to forecast appropriate market supply and demand trends.

In addition to the primary real estate types (i.e., multifamily, office, retail, & industrial), the analyst will evaluate mixed use, senior housing, student housing, tax credit, and lodging properties. While the analyst will focus largely on property level research for individual deals, macro-level industry data analysis is also routinely required for review and reporting of PNC portfolio performance or for macroeconomic reviews. The analyst will serve internal customers; the ability to multi-task and communicate timely and effectively with relationship managers, underwriters, and credit officers is instrumental in allowing PNC to develop an accurate picture of an asset and to issue competitive term sheets to gain new business. As part of the review, interviews of market experts, customers, brokers, leasing agents, and appraisers to get local views on the market are incorporated into the analysis. The analyst then writes a clear and concise summary of the supportive data and analysis for their conclusions/forecasts and presents to senior loan committee in conjunction with the deal team.

Other functions of the REMA group that the analyst may work on include criticized asset valuations, reconciling appraisal findings to internal underwriting, and quarterly sector studies. Appraisal, brokerage, real estate research, urban planning, macroeconomics, real estate property management, lending, or underwriting skills are all relevant. Argus skills are not required but are helpful.

Bachelor's Degree and or an advanced degree plus 3+ years of related experience

Role Summary:
This role sits at the intersection of Design Operations, Product Design, and Design Systems, partnering across Product, Research, Experience Design, UI, and Engineering teams to scale design quality, consistency, and delivery effectiveness.

This role operates horizontally across teams, ensuring that:
• Design systems are adopted and evolved based on real product needs.
• Design workflows are consistent, efficient, and scalable.
• Cross-crew alignment is strong between Design, Product, Research, and Engineering.

This role owns the effectiveness of the design delivery system, ensuring work is properly shaped, routed, governed, and delivered across Research, Experience Design, and Design System teams.

The role serves as an operator, orchestrator, and systems owner responsible for improving how work flows through the organization. This includes defining and optimizing operating models, enabling cross-functional collaboration, driving Design System adoption, and removing friction that slows teams down.
You will partner closely with Design Leadership to define DesignOps strategy while driving execution as a key operator and change agent across the organization.

This is a hands-on senior IC role that blends:
• Design delivery orchestration and operational leadership.
• Design System governance and adoption.
• Product design expertise and selective hands-on execution.
This role is ideal for a senior individual contributor who has experienced the challenges of scaling design organizations and has successfully built systems, processes, and operating models that improve delivery outcomes.

Core Responsibilities:

1. Design Operations & Cross-Crew Orchestration
Design Delivery System Ownership
• Own the health and effectiveness of the design delivery ecosystem across Research, Experience Design, and Design System teams.
• Act as the operational connector across disciplines, ensuring the right work reaches the right team at the right time with clearly defined goals, dependencies, and success criteria.
• Design and optimize workflows, rituals, and operating models both within Design and across Product and Engineering.
• Drive operational consistency while maintaining team agility and delivery velocity.
• Identify organizational friction points and actively remove barriers to execution.

Intake, Work Shaping & Prioritization
• Own and evolve intake and work-shaping processes to ensure initiatives are properly defined, assessed, and routed before entering delivery.
• Partner with leadership on intake management, prioritization, roadmap alignment, and delivery planning.
• Support capacity planning and resource visibility across teams.
• Ensure new work enters the system with appropriate context, ownership, objectives, and success measures.

Stage Gates, Dependencies & Delivery Readiness
• Define and maintain stage gates across discovery, design direction, design system alignment, development readiness, implementation QA, and delivery closure.
• Ensure clear design readiness for development and implementation.
• Surface and manage cross-crew dependencies, blockers, unresolved decisions, and operational risks.
• Establish escalation paths and governance mechanisms to maintain delivery flow and reduce rework.
• Facilitate critiques, working sessions, alignment forums, and operational reviews.

Visibility, Metrics & Continuous Improvement
• Create visibility into:
o What teams are designing.
o Where duplication or divergence is occurring.
o Where Design System opportunities exist.
o Where operational bottlenecks are slowing delivery.
• Define and track Design health metrics, delivery metrics, and Design System adoption measures.
• Monitor and improve the effectiveness of the design delivery system over time.

Success measures may include:
• Reduced design rework.
• Improved design readiness for development.
• Increased Design System adoption.
• Reduced one-off design solutions.
• Improved consistency across product experiences.
• Clearer ownership and accountability.
• Improved delivery flow and reduced operational friction.

2. Design System Ownership & Activation
• Govern, champion, and evolve the Design System in partnership with Design Leadership.
• Co-own the Design System roadmap, including components, tokens, patterns, templates, and supporting assets.
• Define organizational governance models and contribution processes for Design System enhancements.
• Establish clear inclusion criteria for system components versus custom solutions.
• Drive Design System adoption as both a product and operational discipline.
• Partner with Product, Design, and Engineering leaders to align teams around system usage and implementation standards.
• Enable teams through documentation, education, working sessions, office hours, and ongoing support.
• Facilitate Design System audits and adoption reviews to improve consistency across products.
• Support design-to-development parity throughout the implementation lifecycle.
• Partner with engineering teams to improve Design System implementation, scalability, and maintainability.

3. Product Design Leadership & Strategic Execution
• Lead or support select high-impact product initiatives where hands-on design involvement is required.
• Maintain direct exposure to product design work to inform operational improvements and Design System evolution.
• Establish quality benchmarks and best practices through participation in strategic initiatives.
• Create and deliver design concepts, workflows, prototypes, and experience solutions when needed.
• Partner with Product, Research, and Engineering teams to ensure experiences align with user needs and business goals.
• Support user research, usability testing, and iterative design improvements.
• Champion accessibility, usability, and responsive design best practices.
• Serve as a credible design practitioner capable of contributing to and evaluating design work across teams.

Technical Skills:

Must-Have
• Advanced Figma systems expertise (Components, Variants, Variables, Tokens, Libraries)
• Deep experience scaling and governing Design Systems.
• Strong UX and Product Design fundamentals across the end-to-end product lifecycle.
• Proven experience establishing or improving DesignOps functions, workflows, or operating models.
• Strong understanding of:
o Front-end architecture
o Component-based systems
o Responsive design principles
o Design-to-development workflows
• Experience working within Agile product delivery environments.
• Experience supporting cross-functional delivery models at scale.
• Accessibility (WCAG) expertise integrated into design practice.
• Experience defining metrics, performance indicators, and operational measures for design organizations.

Nice-to-Have
• Storybook and Design System tooling ecosystems.
• Design maturity assessment and organizational transformation experience.
• Process optimization, service design, or operating model design experience.
• Analytics and measurement frameworks for adoption, efficiency, and quality.

Soft Skills:

Must-Have
• Operator mindset (not strategist-only, not designer-only).
• Systems thinker who identifies patterns across teams and addresses root causes.
• Strong organizational and operational leadership skills without direct people management.
• Ability to influence peers, leaders, and cross-functional partners.
• Bias toward action, simplification, and continuous improvement.
• Ability to establish standards and governance without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.
• Strong facilitation and alignment-building capabilities.
• Ability to navigate ambiguity and build structure where it does not yet exist.

Nice-to-Have
• High emotional intelligence and organizational awareness.
• Coaching and mentorship mindset.
• Executive communication and stakeholder management experience.
• Change management and organizational design experience.
